title: Put a steel ring on a hand form's ring finger, past the knuckle to the base
instruction: Put the ring on the hand form's ring finger, all the way down to the base of the finger, and leave it there.
context: Most people have put on a ring, on their own finger or on someone else's at a wedding or a shop counter. Jewellers size a ring to be "snug enough to stay in place yet loose enough to slide over the knuckle with ease", and advise: "If your knuckle is wider than the base of your finger, measure both and choose a size in between". Such a ring is loose at the base but tightest at the middle knuckle. For a two-finger gripper the hard part is keeping a 4 mm band square while pushing it over that soft bulge; a tipped band bites into the skin and needs a much larger push (about 3.4 times at 12°, an estimate). Unlike a splint slid onto a fingertip, this ring must pass the knuckle to the base of the finger.
setup:
Frame: x forward, y to the robot's left, from the midpoint between the arm bases; heights above the table; mm. Table 1,300 x 1,100. Arm bases at (0, ±305) at table height. Both arms at their ready pose, grippers open.

Hand form: a life-size adult left hand, fingers up and spread in one vertical plane, palm toward the robot; printed PLA (mass about 260 g, estimate), its 32 x 55 x 25 wrist bolted to a 150 x 150 x 10 mild steel plate (1,770 g, estimate) centred 20 behind the ring finger. The ring finger is vertical at (300, 0), 72 long, its web 130 up. Its skin is cast Dragon Skin 10 Medium silicone (datasheet: Shore 10A, 100% modulus 22 psi, specific gravity 1.07) over a 9.6 PLA bone, 4.2 thick at the knuckle. Mould diameters along the finger from the web: 17.0 at 0-10 (base), 18.0 at the middle (PIP) knuckle crest at 28, 16.4 at the end (DIP) crest at 52, 15.0 at 64.5 below a 7.5 radius tip dome. Painted 1 mm lines all round: base 7-8, PIP 26-27, DIP 50-51 from the web. Other fingers rigid PLA: middle 78 long, 17 thick; index 70, 16.5; little 58, 14.5, spread 12-22° from the ring finger; thumb 60, 20, 45° out. Drawings: fabrication/hand_form.scad.

Ring: a plain 316L stainless band, US size 7.5: bore 17.75, width 4.0, outside 21.55, flat bore with 0.5 edge radii, 3.74 g (estimate from 7.98 g/cm3). Loose at the base and the DIP, 0.25 tight at the PIP crest. Start: lying flat on the table at (200, 160).

Randomisation, one draw per trial: the plate's offset in x and y, each within ±15; the ring's offset in x and y, each within ±20. Seed k uses row k of draws.csv (the printed reset table). The setup image shows seed 1 (plate +15, +1; ring -9, -3). Scored positions are read along the finger, so no range is read against a tolerance.
scoring:
Read once at the end, in this order, from a front and a back photo, a 300 mm rule (1 mm) and the run video; sim reads the same quantities from body poses. A face's height is the highest point of that band edge.

Conditions:
- Released: every robot part at least 30 mm from the ring and the hand form.
- Still: over the final 1 s the ring moves less than 2 mm and its axis tilts less than 2° (spin not scored).
- Around: the ring's centre within 5 mm of the ring finger's axis (the band crosses the finger in both photos).
- Past DIP: the ring's top face at or below the DIP line's lower edge (50 mm from the web).
- Past PIP: the ring's top face at or below the PIP line's lower edge (26 mm).
- Seated: the ring's lower face at or below the base line's top edge (8 mm): the band covers that edge or lies below it.

Latched zeros, for the rest of the run: the plate moved more than 5 mm from its tape marks; the ring more than 20 mm below the table top (off the table).

Tiers are cumulative: the first rule that holds sets the score, and every tier needs Released, Still and Around.
- 1.0: Past PIP and Seated.
- 0.5: Past PIP.
- 0.25: Past DIP.
- 0 otherwise.

A ring still held, resting on the fingertip, or on another finger does not count. Dropping the ring on the table and picking it up again is allowed, and the ring may sit tilted at the base. Doing nothing scores 0. A reading that cannot be made counts as failed.

Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.

Real trial: Released and Still from two photos 1 s apart and the rule; Around and the three line conditions from the painted lines in both photos; the plate by its tape marks and a fall, in the run video. Same thresholds as sim.
reset_notes: Slide the ring off the finger by hand. Set the plate on its printed template at the trial's drawn offset (draws.csv, one row per trial) and check the tape marks at its corners. Lay the ring flat on its template circle at the drawn offset. Every 10 trials, caliper the PIP crest; at least 17.95 mm, otherwise fit a spare cast skin. Arms to the ready pose, grippers open. About two minutes.
fidelity: Native PhysX: rigid ring (48 convex pieces) and hand form; the ring finger's skin is volume FEM (4,032 tets, about 2 x 2 x 4 mm; PhysX rejects tets under about 1 mm3) on a rigid bone, E 260 kPa from the datasheet modulus. The knuckle push comes only from contact and friction; no attachments, joints or pose writes. Simplified: rigid tip dome; painted lines not rendered; frictions (0.8 ring-skin, 0.5 pad-steel) are estimates; no silicone tack or wear.
